llm.summary: This skill is a payment-gated local drafting workflow whose network, credential, and project-fingerprint behavior is mostly disclosed and aligned with its licensing purpose, though users should understand what is sent and stored.

dimensions.detail: The project fingerprint is derived from .git/config, common project metadata files, or the normalized path and only the resulting SHA-256 fingerprint is sent to the fixed payment endpoint; source files and directory listings are not uploaded by the inspected scripts.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill requires the separate clawtip-skill payment prerequisite and provides local Python scripts; no hidden installer, background worker, or automatic package installation was found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill limits remote use to license/order/payment authorization and says draft generation remains local after confirmation, but the scripts themselves perform network requests after notices rather than enforcing an interactive confirmation prompt.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill writes order metadata, including the software fingerprint, under the user's OpenClaw orders directory and later reads a local payment credential for verification; this is persistent but scoped to the payment workflow.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is local software-IP draft generation after per-project payment authorization; filesystem read, outbound network, payment processing, and credential reading are coherent with license checking, order creation, payment verification, and local draft work.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with a fixed remote payment service receiving a hashed project fingerprint for license enforcement and a payment credential for verification. Review the local order files under the OpenClaw orders directory if you want to see retained payment metadata, and expect the QR path may need fixing because the QR display helper is not defined.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: The artifact does inspect project identity inputs and sends a derived fingerprint, but SKILL.md explicitly describes the fingerprint priority and the remote license/order purpose. This is purpose-aligned, though users should note that hashed project identity can still be correlatable.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The undefined _show_qr_code call is a reliability and disclosure issue in the QR payment path, but no hidden QR-rendering implementation or extra data flow exists in the artifact; the script would fail at that point after printing order details.
[SDI-4] expected: The runtime notice saying only minimal payment metadata is sent is incomplete because the software fingerprint is also sent, but SKILL.md separately discloses automatic fingerprinting and the per-software license mechanism. This warrants user guidance rather than a Review verdict.
